gaps.construct: nested def that captures `patterns` from ignore_patterns(*patterns) and is returned as a value to be called later by copytree
gaps.description: The doc has no nested operations, no operation-valued parameters or results, and no capture. The captured variable became a parameter, which changes the function's arity and means copytree's `ignore` callback cannot be expressed at all.
No Set type or conversion to one is in the doc; `Set of Text` and `set_of` were invented.
No in-place extend; `followed by` is only shown in specs, so its use in code (and whether it allocates) is a guess.
No variadic parameters; patterns is a List and callers must build one.

gaps.construct: Python list/set building with implicit allocation
gaps.description: Allocation must be visible, so a 5-line pure-looking helper gains an Allocator parameter, `uses memory` and OutOfMemory.

invented_syntax: followed by used outside a spec
notes: This is the common Python idiom of a factory returning a configured callback; without first-class operations Scribe cannot express the shape, only the body. A designer should decide whether operation values (with capability-checked capture) are a goal or a non-goal with an alternative such as a choice of filter kinds.
